title: Choosing and Routing Models
summary: No single model is the best choice for every request. Production systems pick models on a quality, cost and latency frontier, then cascade or route traffic so that cheap models handle easy requests and expensive ones handle the rest.
objectives: Compare models on a quality, cost and latency frontier and discard dominated options
Compute the cost of a request and of a month of traffic from token counts and prices
Derive the expected cost, quality and latency of a two-model cascade
Choose a router threshold from a labelled evaluation set and compare it with random and oracle routing
Design a routing layer that is observable, version-pinned and budget-aware
prerequisites: You should know what tokens are and how they are priced ([Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization)), what TTFT and TPOT mean ([Measuring Inference](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference)), and how to build an evaluation set with a pass rate ([Success Criteria](/learn/evaluation/success-criteria)).
